01 / DECISION

Mordum Extreme

The difficulty line was set too high

6 notes
REPORTED CLEAR RATE3.47% → 33.09%
AVERAGE CLEARER COMBAT SCORE9,664 → 9,121

Why release it this way?

Mordum was intended to fill a quieter content period with a distinctive challenge. The team knew classes had advantages and disadvantages, but decided to launch without raid-specific compensation after promising to draw a difficulty line.

What went wrong?

Geum Kang-seon said Jeon Jae-hak’s intended difficulty threshold ended up higher than intended. Class differences then created situations where groups could not clear. Setting that threshold incorrectly was the biggest failure.

Why the emergency nerf?

Leaving it unchanged would miss the intended purpose; nerfing it would disadvantage early clearers. A faster decision would have been better. He described this as a failure rather than an issue they had been unaware of, and said insufficiently detailed planning led to the emergency nerf.

No extension. No further nerfs.

He rejected extending Mordum’s availability and said there would be no additional nerfs. The team should learn from this and improve the next content release.

Clear results after the nerf

The reported clear rate rose from 3.47% to 33.09% as of the evening of October 15. Average Combat Score among players who cleared fell from 9,664 to 9,121. The clear-rate population was not specified.

An apology to players

He apologised for the sense of loss caused by Mordum. “Drawing a line” had been ambiguous: players naturally expect the line to fall behind their own position, and there is no threshold everyone will agree on.

02 / DIRECTION

Class balance & supports

Synergies need attention

6 notes

Ark Grid makes balancing harder

Ark Grid has made class balance more difficult, while also limiting how freely players can change their builds. Repeating that the team will work harder is no longer enough.

Party synergies and excess Crit Rate

Party-synergy changes are being worked on, with Crit Rate synergies the priority. Many classes can already reach high Crit Rate, reducing the value of additional Crit Rate in those parties. Players should not have to wait long, but no exact patch date was given.

Support direction must come first

Support player skill has an increasingly large effect on the damage of the other party members, especially in Mordum Extreme. This creates pressure and frustration for both supports and DPS players. The team has not yet settled on a direction.

Two possible directions for supports

One option is to retain strong support influence while raising the performance floor—for example, making it easier to maintain high uptime on brand and other buffs. Another is to reduce support buff strength while changing the gameplay around it. These are discussion examples, not announced nerfs or automatic-buff changes; other solutions remain possible.

System-level alternatives were discussed

If class balance cannot be solved adequately, broader systems could be considered—for example, adjustments within a base-class family. This was a hypothetical example, not an announcement of a class-change ticket or a confirmed system.

No balance patch before Kazeros Extreme

The post says no advance balance patch is planned before Kazeros Extreme.

03 / OPINION

Raid design & cadence

More breathing room between major releases

6 notes

DPS differences across raids

The stream showed the spread between maximum and minimum DPS for each gate. Mordum (Act 3) had a larger spread; Belgardin had a much smaller one. Numeric DPS values were not displayed because the material was prepared in a hurry. A smaller spread alone does not prove a raid is well designed.

What is working?

The discussion described raids through Belgardin Nightmare as enjoyable and suggested that skipping Mordum and releasing only Kazeros Extreme might have been a better choice. Damage windows have improved, the developers have gained experience, and frustrating aspects of older raids have been reduced.

Where players gave up

Brelshaza Gate 1 (Narok)’s difficulty was cited as a breaking point. Geum Kang-seon felt many players may already have dropped off in Brelshaza, before reaching Mordum.

Preparing specifically for Mordum

He personally felt Mordum was worth challenging, but that preparations such as an Ark Grid setup suited to Mordum were needed.

Three months versus six months

He considered a three-month major-update cycle a poor choice and suggested roughly six months instead, supported by horizontal content between releases. This was his view, not a confirmed release schedule.

Avoiding both overload and long droughts

A long-running MMORPG should have waves of activity, with players returning over time. The game should avoid both excessively quiet periods and overwhelming amounts of content.

04 / DISCUSSION

Gold economy

Supply rose faster than spending

6 notes

The core issue: content release speed

He linked abrupt drops in gold’s value to the pace of content releases. Faster raid releases raise gold generation, while gold spending has not kept up.

Why it is difficult to correct

Adding spending can make the game feel more expensive, but new raids are also expected to offer higher gold rewards. Quickly cutting rewards then provokes the reaction that the content is already being nerfed.

The economic effect arrives later

Doubling rewards in endgame content does not immediately collapse the economy. The delayed impact becomes much stronger when generating that gold becomes easy at a very low entry threshold.

Cash-shop packages

The reported figures are his estimate that currencies introduced through packages account for around 2% of the economic impact. No detailed methodology is included.

Existing progression investments

Asked about new spending content, he said his understanding was that the direction is to protect the value of existing systems.

Horizontal players have declined

The number of players who engage with horizontal content without raiding has fallen significantly. The stream included a trend chart comparing horizontal-content users who raid with those who do not.

05 / TENTATIVE

Same-class rosters & the six-character limit

A clearer position is expected this winter

7 notes

What same-class alt rosters means

This refers to rosters with several characters of the same class, allowing players to move gems between those characters and reduce gearing costs. The discussion concerns duplicate-class alt rosters, rather than every player with alts.

The share shown on stream

The reported figures are 2.1% in summer 2023, 6.0% in summer 2024, 16.0% in summer 2025, and 17.8% in summer 2026. It does not precisely define the denominator for this share.

Why same-class rosters became attractive

Season 3 introduced many systems for optimizing characters, increasing the cost of progression. Reusing gems across characters of the same class reduces that cost, giving players a financial reason to build duplicate-class rosters.

Why the team did not intervene earlier

Geum Kang-seon felt the start of Season 3 would have been a better time for Jeon Jae-hak to address the issue. Unexpected risks were cited as the reason action was not taken then. Those risks were not specified, and no particular restriction was announced.

Adjustment, not eradication

He questioned whether gem costs should effectively push MMORPG players into repeating the same class. But players have built these rosters without a clear prior stance from the developer. He said the position should be clarified this winter and described adjustment rather than eliminating the playstyle.

Six gold-earning characters

The six-character restriction can discourage players from trying new classes. The discussion concerned economic incentives and the motivation to raise a new character. Adjustments appear to be in preparation for winter, with more to be discussed in the follow-up broadcast before LOA ON. Removal of the limit has not been announced.

06 / KR PLANS

Upcoming KR plans

What to watch next

5 notes

Eighth-anniversary broadcast · November 8

November 8 is the reported date for the Korean eighth-anniversary broadcast. Final scheduling is subject to an official announcement.

Follow-up discussion · before November 7

A broadcast provisionally described as “Is Lost Ark okay as it is?” was teased for roughly two weeks later, before November 7, with the three lead developers. It will precede LOA ON and discuss issues including roster restrictions. Plenty of new content was also teased.

A new class is being prepared for December

Changes are being prepared alongside the six-character restriction. This is a class players had often requested even during Geum Kang-seon’s time. The class identity has not been revealed.

New-class release timing

He suggested reconsidering the timing of new classes and taking time to sort out existing issues rather than always adding another class.

Aldebaran Sea (upcoming KR region)

The clarification was that it is not endgame content, rather than simply dismissing it as side content. The recap author suggests that the team did not want to open a largely empty sea with too few islands. The new KR city, provisionally transliterated as Lasamoa, is described as a major city, with connected content elsewhere and an expanded scale. Western names for these upcoming locations have not been confirmed.

07 / CLARIFICATION

Leadership, QA & development

Jeon Jae-hak remains the director

5 notes

Why Geum Kang-seon appeared

Jeon Jae-hak is still the director. Geum Kang-seon appeared to communicate with players. He had been reading the community and saw resignation more than anger; he felt the broadcast could not wait beyond this week. He opened with a light remark about whether he could tell viewers to order chicken.

QA exists, but this testing fell short

He said there is a sizeable QA team, but testing was insufficient this time. He could not simply claim everything was going well and would review the accumulated development steps and processes.

His view of Jeon Jae-hak

He believed Jeon would do well when handing over the position. Systems such as elixirs and the ambition of later raids made him feel the younger team had achieved things he might not have attempted himself. The worsening mood appears to have been difficult for Jeon too.

Turning a mocked slogan into reality

He acknowledged the community’s mocking use of “In game is a party.” Like the old “Are you still playing that game?” sentiment, he wants the phrase to become sincerely positive.

Has staffing been cut?

He said staffing has increased overall since open beta. Although the team recently lost three or four people, he considered headcount broadly maintained. The issue is direction, not simply the number of developers. He believes more content is being produced than in his time and said the team puts in substantial hours.
